about.title: A little about me
paragraphs: I've always been drawn to computers. It started with gaming and online communities like Reddit, X, and Discord, later turned into studying Computer Science, and that's how I ended up in IT.
I like that the result of my work is visible right away — that's the best part.

I'm a fairly calm and introverted person. I don't need to be the loudest person in the room, but if I see a problem or have an idea that could improve something, I say so directly. I usually listen and analyse first, and only then speak up.

After work I'm still often at the computer — I'm into new tech, sports, football, and games. This isn't just an eight-hour job for me. I follow the internet, trends, and where the industry is heading on my own, simply because it interests me and I like knowing what's happening and where it's all going. That curiosity also matters in my work: it helps me tell short-lived hype apart from solutions that actually make sense.

I see AI as more than a ready-made tool for generating text or code. I'm interested in local LLMs, the differences between models, their capabilities, limitations, context, how they work, and their trade-offs.
With this many years in the industry and so many projects behind me, I can simply feel when something will work and when it won't — and that's where people have a huge advantage over AI.
